latin: Licet dei uoluntas consequens semper impleatur, non tamen necessitatem rebus uolitis generaliter imponit.
translation: Even though God's consequent will is always accomplished, it does not thereby impose necessity across the board on the things willed.
translation_note: 'uoluntas consequens': God's will as it bears on the actual outcome, as opposed to his antecedent will. Sense checked against farmer1998:11383.
